key_insight: On-policy distillation updates are not large or widespread; they are small, coordinate-sparse, and spread across layers, often concentrating in feed-forward network (FFN) channels. This suggests OPD changes models in a highly targeted way despite using dense teacher supervision.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of understanding of how on-policy distillation actually modifies model parameters during post-training, especially the relationship between dense supervision and the geometry/sparsity of resulting updates.
method: Analyze on-policy distillation across multiple language and vision-language model pairs and tasks.
Measure update sparsity and geometric properties of parameter changes during training.
Compare how OPD-style updates distribute across layers and parameter groups, with attention to FFN-heavy concentration.
impact: For practitioners, this helps explain why OPD can be effective and where its learning signal is applied. It can guide more efficient distillation designs, parameter-focused diagnostics, and future methods that exploit sparse update patterns.
visual_elements: A layer-wise heatmap showing where parameter updates are concentrated
A sparsity plot comparing dense teacher supervision vs sparse student parameter changes
A model diagram highlighting FFN channels as major update hotspots
A before-and-after geometry visualization of update directions in parameter space
paper_title: Dense Supervision, Sparse Updates: On the Sparsity and Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
paper_authors: Guo Yu, Wenlin Liu, Yulan Hu, Hao-Xuan Ma, Jun-Peng Jiang
